RPE is "rate of perceived exertion," a 1 to 10 scale for how hard a set felt. RPE 8 means you finished the set with about 2 reps still in the tank. You could have squeezed out two more, but not three.

It's useful because it adjusts for your day. A weight that's an 8 when you're fresh might be a 9 after a bad night's sleep, and the scale lets you train to the effort instead of chasing a fixed number. If you're unsure whether a set was an 8, ask yourself how many more clean reps you could have done, with form holding up.
